title: Active-active edge gateway failover and session-aware traffic shifting
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Problem: Hosted API edge currently uses active-passive regional failover and DNS-based routing for long-lived connections (streaming sessions). During region outages we observe increased tail latency, connection drops for streaming and streaming sessions that depend on per-edge state (stream tokens, KV cache warmups). Goals: (1) implement active-active edge deployment with deterministic traffic shifting that preserves streaming sessions and minimizes client-visible disconnects; (2) ensure SLOs (p99 latency < 200ms for text gen, availability 99.95%) are respected during failover; (3) integrate circuit breakers and load-shedding rules at the edge to protect origin capacity; (4) provide operational runbooks and dashboards for on-call to exercise controlled failovers.
background: We run edge gateways in three regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) and route clients via nearest-region policies. Current issues: DNS TTLs and client reconnection semantics cause slow failovers; sticky session approaches using metaload balancer cookies conflict with streaming (WebSocket/TCP) which needs connection affinity; our KV cache (prefix caching, model kv) is local to region leading to cache cold-start amplification on failover. Recent incident INC-2026-01 highlighted cascading overload when a single region regressed under load and other regions accepted bursts without load-shedding, exceeding Dedicated capacity and leading to degraded p99s.
acceptance_criteria: Active-active routing enabled across at least two regions with non-DNS traffic shifting (BGP/Anycast+edge routing or control-plane HTTP routing)
Streaming session resilience: <1% client disconnects observed during simulated region CPU outage with connection draining enabled
Session affinity semantics defined and implemented for streaming: tokens are valid in another region for handoff within 60s window
Circuit breaker rules in edge: per-tenant and global thresholds with exponential backoff and clear metrics emitted
Automated load-shedding policy that reduces low-priority requests under overload while preserving SLOs for high-priority traffic
Runbook documented and tested with a canary failover drill (drill postmortem attached)
tasks: Design: define session token format and region-transfer TTL (Leah)
Runtime: add edge-side circuit breaker with sliding-window error-rate and latency metrics (ENG)
API: extend control plane to signal traffic-shift percentages and draining windows
KV cache: implement async cross-region warmup + best-effort prefetch for hot keys
Streaming: implement connection handoff flow for 60s transient window using rehydrate token
Testing: run chaos test traffic shifting for 3 failure modes (CPU spike, network partition, process restart)
Metrics: add SLO dashboard (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability, backend queue length, circuit-breaker trips)
decisions: Use active-active model with control-plane driven traffic percentages instead of DNS-only failover to reduce client reconnection variance
Adopt short-lived rehydrate tokens carryable across regions (signed JWT with region claim and 'handoff' flag) to allow streaming handoff
Circuit breaker strategy: two-tier breakers (edge local per-tenant + global edge safeguard) with automatic backoff and operator override
Load-shedding priority: rank requests by customer tier + request type (streaming control + safety checks highest), shed embeddings/batch lower-priority when overloaded
KV cache replication: do not aim for strict consistency during failover — use best-effort async replication and accept potential cold starts while preserving correctness
implementation_notes: Edge will expose a small control endpoint to consume traffic-shift directives from the control plane (percentages + drain window). Streaming clients will receive a short rehydrate token in the next streaming heartbeat that can be used to re-establish in another region. Connection draining will gracefully refuse new streams for the configured drain window while keeping existing streams alive and allowing token handoff. Circuit breakers implemented with a 60s sliding window and minimum request volume to avoid noisy trips. Load-shedding uses a token-bucket per-edge and per-tenant; when bucket exhausted, respond with 429 and 'retry-after' plus fallback model hint. All emitted metrics must include tags: region, edge-id, tenant, model, pathway (stream|rpc|embed).
testing_plan: Unit tests for rehydrate token creation/validation and expiry semantics
Integration test simulating client moving from us-west to us-east during an artificial us-west CPU spike
Load test: ramp 2x baseline across both regions with synthetic streaming sessions to measure p99 and connection loss
Chaos: network partition test that isolates backend from one region while shifting 40% traffic to the other region and verifying circuit breaker behavior
Canary rollout: enable active-active for 5% of traffic, observe metrics for 48 hours before 25% rollout
observability: Dashboards: edge-failover-overview, per-region-slo, streaming-session-health. Alerts: p99 latency for text-gen > 200ms for 15m; availability drop > 0.2%; circuit-breaker trip rate > 1% for 5m. Tracing: attach span for 'control-plane-traffic-shift' and 'rehydration' flows. Logs: structured events on token handoff, drain start/complete, load-shedding decision with reason code.
runbook: Runbook steps: (1) verify control-plane health and current shift percentages; (2) trigger manual shift to drain region (set drain window 120s) and monitor streaming-session-handbacks; (3) if p99 spikes, trigger edge circuit-breaker and rollback traffic-shift; (4) escalate to SRE if availability < 99.9% after rollback. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Edge+Failover+Runbook
